26.0.0.en: 1- Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD without wavering.

26.0.1.en: Without wavering: with steadfastness and without being shaken.

26.0.2.en: 1- David says to God, "Judge", that is, judge, O God, with justice; for You are different from unjust men, You are just and know the secrets of hearts, that is, You know my innocence. It is a taking refuge in God by prayer, that He may rescue him from the words of the wicked.

26.0.3.en: 2- David declares his innocence of the accusations brought against him, and shows his walking in integrity, that is, in God's commandments, and by integrity he means the relative perfection that God allows him. This is not pride on David's part but a defense of his innocence.

26.0.4.en: 3- Before the false accusations David had nothing to do but take refuge in God, trust in Him and abide in Him, because He is the only true refuge of all who are wronged. And this proves his humility and that he is weak and took refuge in God to defend him, and therefore by his saying "in mine integrity" he does not mean that he trusts in his own righteousness.

26.0.5.en: 4- David's taking refuge in God answers the accusations brought against him that he left the house of the Lord and joined the pagans.

26.0.6.en: 5- David's walking in integrity declares the purity of his heart and his forgiveness of those who wronged and abused him, such as Saul and Absalom.

26.1.0.en: 2- Prove me, O LORD, and try me; purify my kidneys and my heart.

26.1.1.en: 1- David accepted the trials that came upon him and did not murmur or ask why these trials, unlike Job, who protested against God, and this shows David's submission to God.

26.1.2.en: 2- David asked God to try him with these trials, not meaning that God should know his purity, for God knows everything. But he means that God should try him so that David may know himself and discover his faults in order to treat them by God's power, just as gold is tested by fire to rid it of dross, or impurities; therefore David said "purify" my heart and my kidneys, that is, the depths of my soul, so that it may be perfectly pure.

26.1.3.en: 3- The word of God examines man and tries him and reveals the secrets of his heart, that he may be purified from all evil.

26.1.4.en: 4- David's saying "prove me, try me, purify" declares his confidence in the purity of his heart toward those who wronged him, and his readiness, if any evil is found, that God purify him from it.

26.1.5.en: 5- The kidneys and the heart are inner organs, so they represent the depths of David that he seeks to have purified, especially since the kidneys purify the blood of toxins, and the heart distributes the pure blood to nourish all the organs of the body. So if the kidneys and the heart are examined and purified, the whole person is pure.

26.2.0.en: 3- For thy lovingkindness is before mine eyes: and I have walked in thy truth.

26.2.1.en: 1- David always looks to God's mercy, so he is then able to accept trial and bear it, because God's mercy supports him and strengthens him.

26.2.2.en: 2- When David looks to God's mercy he remembers God's care for him throughout his life, that is, that God's mercy was always with him, so his heart is assured, and he even praises God.

26.2.3.en: 3- David's walking in the truth gives him courage to come forward asking for God's mercy, because God has mercy on His children who keep His rights.

26.2.4.en: 4- David's declaring his walking in the truth is a defense of himself against the accusations that he separated from the people of God and refused worship in the house of God. He was compelled to flee from the face of Saul, but he holds fast to the rights of God and His commandments.

26.2.5.en: 5- David's thinking is directed toward God; he walks in His truth and asks for His mercy, and has no feelings against his enemies. He does not ask God to vindicate him at their expense, or to punish them, but is concerned with his inner purity and the salvation of his soul. And this is the conduct of God's children.

26.3.0.en: 4- I have not sat with vain persons, neither will I go in with dissemblers.

26.3.1.en: 5- I have hated the congregation of evildoers; and will not sit with the wicked.

26.3.2.en: 1- They accused David of living among the pagans and separating from the people of God, and David affirms here his goodness and righteousness in that he did not mingle, and also kept away from the wicked and hated their evils; that is, even among the pagans he took care to sit with God's righteous children, who accompanied him in his flight.

26.3.3.en: 2- David declares his keeping away from sinners in every form; he kept away from

26.3.8.en: 3- David not only kept away from the wicked, but also from his heart hated and rejected evil in all its forms, and his heart was not attached to it; that is, he kept a heart pure toward God, as in the preceding verse he asked for God to examine his heart that it might be pure.

26.3.9.en: 4- David refused to mingle with the dissemblers, who pretended to piety but whose hearts were full of evil. And this shows David's carefulness about those with whom he mingles, and God's guidance of him.

26.3.10.en: Be careful about those with whom you mingle; for if they are God's children they will be an encouragement to you on the way of life with God. And if they are among the wicked, keep away from them, even if you have an old relationship with them. Do not gamble with the salvation of your soul and your eternity out of shyness before these wicked friends or relatives.

26.4.s.en: (2) Proof of his love for the house of the Lord

26.4.0.en: 6- I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O LORD:

26.4.1.en: 1- David said "I will wash mine hands in innocency" because he looked with his heart at what happens in the Tabernacle of Meeting, where the priests wash their hands in the laver before offering the sacrifices for the people; he longs in his heart to share with the priests in washing his hands, to be purified from every sin. And although he is far from the Temple because of his flight from the face of Saul, his heart is attached to the worship offered in the Temple.

26.4.2.en: 2- The hands signify works, so David's washing his hands in innocency means the purity of his works from all evil, since he did not mingle with the pagans around him and did not share with them in their sins.

26.4.3.en: 3- The priests used to go around the bronze altar before offering the burnt offerings and sacrifices upon it. And the one who offered the sacrifice shared with the priest in going around the altar. And David longs to be in the Temple, to go around the altar on which sacrifices are offered for the forgiveness of sin. He longs for God to forgive him his sins.

26.4.4.en: 4- Washing the hands is a well-known ancient custom, by which a person demonstrates his innocence of any charge that may be attributed to him. So David's washing his hands in innocency is a declaration of his innocence of the charges brought against him, which are his mingling with the pagans and his rejection of worship in the Temple.

26.4.5.en: 5- Washing the hands for us in the New Testament takes place in the sacraments of Baptism and confession. As for going around the altar, the priest and the deacon do it in the Liturgy on behalf of the people in circuits accompanied by prayers, and it declares the bond with the altar and the readiness to receive the sacrament of Communion. And the priest recites this verse when he washes his hands during the Liturgy, to declare the purity of his heart, so that he may be able to touch the Body and Blood of the Lord.

26.5.0.en: 7- That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works.

26.5.1.en: 1- David continues in his longings toward the Temple, and while far from it he hears the sounds of praise offered to God (thanksgiving), which the Levites chant. And if the Levites are silent, he hears in the spirit the praises of the angels around God who dwells in His Temple. And he longs to share with them in praising and thanking God.

26.5.2.en: 2- When David hears the praises his heart is moved, so he shares with them by mentioning the wonders of God, that is, he thanks God for His kindnesses, praises Him, and declares his attachment to the worship of God and his separation from the worship of the pagans.

26.5.3.en: 3- David's hearing the voice of praise (thanksgiving), in spite of his distance from the Temple, is evidence of his purity, his strong relationship with God and his distance from sin.

26.6.0.en: 8- LORD, I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth.

26.6.1.en: 1- David always thinks of the house of the Lord, which is the Tabernacle of Meeting, and therefore his heart was attached to it and loved it, so it became the most important thing in his life.

26.6.2.en: 2- David sees God dwelling in His house with great glory, so he was occupied with Him instead of all material things and the glories of the world, and his longings for Him increased, and he lived in it in the spirit, even if he was far from it in the body.

26.6.3.en: How beautiful is your attachment to the house of the Lord, as you behold in it His glory and enjoy His presence, not only when you partake of the Holy Sacraments but also at times when there are no liturgical prayers; for the Church is always full of the glory of God and His saints.

26.7.0.en: 9- Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men:

26.7.1.en: 10- In whose hands is mischief, and their right hand is full of bribes.

26.7.2.en: 1- David asks God to separate him from the wicked, who commit sin and are hard of heart, so they shed the blood of the innocent and pervert justice by bribery. He means that his heart and feelings be separated from them, that he may live for God in his thought, feelings and works.

26.7.3.en: 2- David means above all that his place on the Day of Judgment be far from the wicked, that is, that he enjoy eternal life with God far from eternal torment; because he separated from the wicked on earth, he asks for separation from them in eternity.

26.7.4.en: 3- David was not concerned with the accusations brought against him that he mingled with the wicked and kept away from God, but his whole concern was God's look at him and what God sees in him; as long as God is pleased with him and knows the purity of his heart, he has his place in the Kingdom.

26.7.5.en: 4- David did not ask for revenge on the wicked, or on those who falsely accuse him, or for any position on earth, or earthly lusts. His only concern was his relationship with God and his place in the Kingdom.

26.8.0.en: 11- But as for me, I will walk in mine integrity: redeem me, and be merciful unto me.

26.8.1.en: 1- His request in the two preceding verses was negative, that is, his asking to keep away from the wicked. But here he makes a positive request, which is to obtain divine redemption and mercy, because he is a sinner and in need of God's mercy and forgiveness.

26.8.2.en: 2- In spite of David's being among the wicked, he walked in his integrity, that is, in God's commandments. And he does not mean his walking in integrity as a boast, because immediately afterward he asks for God's redemption and mercy, out of his sense that he is a sinner; but he only means his holding fast to God's commandments, so that no one may stumble because of him.

26.8.3.en: 3- David affirms here that salvation is accomplished by God's redemption and mercy, and not only by human striving and walking in integrity; rather it becomes clear that God's mercy and redemption are granted to those who strive spiritually, and are not granted to the slothful.

26.9.0.en: 12- My foot standeth in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the LORD.

26.9.1.en: 1- When David asked for God's redemption and mercy, God granted him peace, although he was excluded and a fugitive and did not enjoy seeing the house of the Lord, but he felt rest, as if he were standing on a plain and not among the mountains and heights.

26.9.2.en: 2- The even place signifies the way of the Kingdom, in which God set David. And this confirms David's assurance, which drives him to spiritual striving until he reaches heaven.

26.9.3.en: 3- David longs to stand in the midst of the congregations coming to worship God in the Tabernacle of Meeting, and this means David's attachment to the house of the Lord. And this verse shows the importance of communal prayer in the Church.

26.9.4.en: 4- This verse shows David's love for the whole world; he longs that they believe in God and gather together to praise Him (the congregations), and this includes the Jews who believe in God, and signifies the believers in Christ in every place, who pray and praise God, who redeemed them on the Cross.

26.9.5.en: 5- This verse shows the faith of David, who felt that his request was answered, and that he stands on an even place and in the midst of the congregation and blesses God, although he is still scattered and a fugitive in the wildernesses.

26.9.6.en: Be careful to love all people, but keep away from the wicked in their gatherings, their works and their words, so that you keep the purity of your heart, gain God's good pleasure, and then obtain your place in heaven.

26.9.7.en: Faith in the Lord the Savior. Of David. "The LORD is my light and my salvation" (v. 1). Introduction:

26.9.8.en: 1- Its writer is David the prophet

26.9.9.en: 2- When was it written? There are two opinions:

26.9.10.en: a - When David was fleeing from Saul. This is evidenced by what is written in the title of this Psalm in the Septuagint translation, where it is said, "A Psalm of David before he was anointed." It is known that David was anointed king three times: the first when he was sixteen years old, secretly in his father's house, the second when he reigned over the tribe of Judah in Hebron at the age of thirty, and the third when he reigned over all the tribes of Israel at the age of thirty-seven (1 Sam 16:13; 2 Sam 2:5: 3). And what is meant by "before he was anointed" is before his anointing at the age of thirty, that is, the second time. Thus David wrote this Psalm during his flight from the face of Saul.

26.9.11.en: b - When he was fleeing from the face of Absalom his son.

26.9.12.en: 3- This Psalm suits the righteous person who faces tribulations, or the Church suffering persecutions; it is a Psalm that comforts and strengthens God's children during their tribulation.

26.9.13.en: 4- This Psalm shows God as a strong fortress for His children, and that He is able to save them from all tribulations.

26.9.14.en: 5- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Prime; it is a Psalm that strengthens God's children at the beginning of their day, when they remember the Resurrection of Christ, so they rise with Him in power and go out to their lives with vigor and confidence.

27.0.0.en: 1- The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

27.0.1.en: 1- David, who believes in God, feels that He is the light of his life, and therefore purifies him from all the darkness of sin, so he leaves all evils. Therefore when a person prays this Psalm at the beginning of the dawn of the new day he feels that God is the true light that illumines his life.

27.0.2.en: 2- David also feels that God is his Savior from all his tribulations, so he fears no enemy however strong; for who can stand before God, who is able to do all things? It is a wonderful confidence and faith inside David's heart, which gives him complete assurance. And no one can utter these words except one who has trusted in God and emptied himself and humbled himself, so that he can feel the strong hand of God, which overcomes all enemies.

27.0.3.en: 3- David believes that his taking refuge in God by prayer is like his entering a fortress that cannot be stormed, so he laughs at his enemies, and they are terrified of him, while he does not fear them or tremble before them.

27.0.4.en: 4- David has experienced God's work in his life; therefore he says my light, my salvation, and the stronghold of my life; and so we find him speaking with surpassing confidence. And because he enjoys God's presence continually, fear cannot come near him.

27.1.0.en: 2- When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell.

27.1.1.en: 1- David declares that he was exposed to attack by the wicked; he passed through many tribulations that brought him to the point of death. But he says with confidence that the wicked wanted to eat his flesh, but they cannot reach his spirit; their authority is limited, that is, only over the body. Therefore he does not fear them, as Christ said, "Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell" (Mt 10:28).

27.1.2.en: 2- In spite of the cruelty of the wicked and their attempt to destroy David, they were not able to, but stumbled and fell, that is, they failed in their attempt to destroy him, and their weakness also appeared before him, as Saul fell into David's hand twice while pursuing him, but David spared him and did not kill him (1 Sam 24:6, 1 Sam 26:11, 12).

27.1.3.en: 3- David, when his enemies stumbled and fell before him, signifies Christ, before whom His enemies fell when they came to arrest Him in the garden of Gethsemane (Jn 18:4-6).

27.2.0.en: 3- Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.

27.2.1.en: 1- David's faith appears in his assurance if an army attacks him or war rises against him. He did not specify the kind of enemy, or his weapons, or his strength, because he relies on God, who is able to defeat any enemy or any army.

27.2.2.en: 2- These words also apply to spiritual warfare; if the armies of the demons, or various kinds of wars, rise against the spiritual person, his heart is not troubled, because of his confidence that God is stronger than Satan, and God is able to expose his tricks, and has authority over him, so He always gives His children the victory.

27.2.3.en: Persevere in your spiritual striving, and do not be troubled by the devil's wars or the multitude of your falls, for in the end you are guaranteed by God's power the victory over Satan. Hold fast to your spiritual rule, and humble yourself before God and people, and the devil will be shattered before you.

27.2.4.en: (2) The house of the Lord is my fortress (vv. 4-6).

27.3.0.en: 4- One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to gaze intently in his temple.

27.3.1.en: Gaze intently: look carefully, or examine.

27.3.2.en: 1- Although David suffers many pains and needs while he is pursued from the face of Saul, or Absalom, he did not ask anything of God except to dwell and settle in the house of the Lord. And this clearly shows that he is a spiritual person whose heart is attached to the love of God before everything.

27.3.3.en: 2- David's longings are not only to offer worship to God in His house, or to pray before Him, but his heart longs to dwell and abide in the house of the Lord, to enjoy being constantly in His hands; he declares his constant need of God.

27.3.4.en: 3- The beauty of the Lord that David wishes to behold is the sense of His presence, His fear, and the feeling of the holiness and purity that are in His house; he does not mean fine, beautiful sights in the house of the Lord, but the sense of His presence. The gazing is not at the beauty of the Temple, because David knows well everything in the Temple, but he examines the attributes of God who dwells in the Temple, such as holiness and purity, in order to live and thank God for His support of him throughout his life, so his attachment to Him increases.

27.3.5.en: 4- The concern of David the prophet for the house of the Lord appeared not only in these words but also in his concern to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord back to Jerusalem (2 Sam 6:1-6). And when God refused that David build a house for the Lord, and said to him that his son Solomon is the one who would build the house, he then hastened to prepare the building materials of gold, silver, timber and all the needs (1 Chr 22).

27.3.6.en: 5- It was not the custom of the priests or the kings to dwell permanently in the house of the Lord, but David's heart's attachment to the house of the Lord made him wish to dwell in the house of the Lord, in order to live with God, and suffer every day in His holiness; he is not content with offering worship and performing the religious rites, but wants always, every day, to contemplate the beauty of God. And if he cannot dwell in the house of the Lord as a building in which he stays, then at least he dwells there spiritually, that is, he always feels his presence in God's hands, while dwelling in any place.

27.3.7.en: 6- David's longings to dwell in the house of the Lord are not limited to the Tabernacle of Meeting, but he longs to be in the presence of God in heaven, to enjoy the beauty that cannot be expressed.

27.3.8.en: 7- David wants to dwell in the house of the Lord to worship Him at all times, because those devoted to worship, such as Simeon the elder and Anna the prophetess, are the ones who stayed in the house of the Lord (Lk 2:25-40), and this shows his love for the worship of the Lord.

27.3.9.en: 8- David's love of dwelling in the house of the Lord and beholding and gazing intently in His temple implicitly declares his love for communal worship; although he loves individual prayer and prays seven times a day, he also loves praying with his believing brethren in the house of the Lord.

27.3.10.en: 9- David wished to dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of his life. This shows two things:

27.3.11.en: a - His great love for prayer and for being in the house of the Lord.

27.3.12.en: b - His sense of the luminosity of being in the house of the Lord; therefore he said the days of my life and not the nights of my life, and this agrees with the beginning of the Psalm, when he said "The LORD is my light"; he feels God as the light of the world when he stands before Him in His temple.

27.4.0.en: 5- For in the day of evil he shall hide me in his canopy: he shall cover me with the covering of his tent; he shall lift me up upon a rock.

27.4.1.en: 1- The canopy is what they set up during war for the king to sit under in the midst of his army, with a group of mighty soldiers around him to protect him. So David declares here that God is the one who hid him and protected him in the canopy, using the soldiers, and this shows the extent of David's vision of God and his faith that He is his fortress.

27.4.2.en: 2- During the day the heat in summer is intense; therefore a person takes refuge in the tent to be sheltered inside it, and in the rainy winter he also hides in it from the rain and the cold. And David feels that God shelters him in the tent; indeed David also shelters in God's tent, in which is the ark of the covenant, when he takes refuge in Him by prayer, fortifying himself by prayer in His tent.

27.4.3.en: 3- The rock signifies Christ, that is, the strong God, who cannot be penetrated, so when David fortifies himself upon it his enemy cannot reach him.

27.4.4.en: 4- David represents the spiritual person who progresses in his spiritual life: he hides in the canopy, which covers his head, then shelters inside the tent where people do not see him, because he is within the embrace of God. And in the end he reaches the rock upon which he is lifted up, which is the complete, firm fortress that the devil cannot penetrate, because the rock has no doors or windows.

27.4.5.en: 5- The canopy and the tent signify the Incarnation of Christ, who hid His divinity in our body that is subject to change by death, like the canopy and the tent that are moved from place to place. And our hiding and our enlightenment in Christ is accomplished through our partaking of His Body and Blood; He hides Himself under the appearances of bread and wine to give us the greatest power in the world that gives us victory over all our enemies.

27.4.6.en: 6- When Moses desired to see God, He hid him in a cleft in the rock (Ex 33:22), and then he enjoyed seeing God and his face shone. So everyone who takes refuge in Christ the Rock receives the sight and vision of God, that is, he experiences the Kingdom while on earth.

27.4.7.en: 7- When God's people thirsted in the wilderness of Sinai and were exposed to death, Moses struck the rock, and it brought forth water and the people drank. And the Rock was Christ, as the Apostle Paul said (1 Cor 10:4); so whoever takes refuge in Christ is watered by the work of the Holy Spirit in him.

27.4.8.en: 8- The canopy, the tent and the rock signify the Church; the Church is a canopy in which the believer hides from the arrows of the enemy, and he shelters in the tent from the heat of the day, that is, trials, and is lifted up upon the rock, that is, enjoys God's work in him.

27.4.9.en: 9- The rock signifies the strong, firm faith that we enjoy if we always live in Christ.

27.5.0.en: 6- And now shall mine head be lifted up above mine enemies round about me: therefore will I offer in his tabernacle sacrifices of shouting; I will sing, yea, I will sing praises unto the LORD.

27.5.1.en: 1- Since David experienced hiding in the Lord's canopy, sheltering in His tent, and then being lifted up upon His rock, he cried out in faith, declaring that God has lifted him above his enemies, that is, given him victory over them, and honored him with great honor. So he moved from a weak person needing protection to a person strong in God, receiving honor before people and triumphing over those who try to wrong him; that is, he became confident in himself, and thankful to God, who made him great.

27.5.2.en: 2- When he felt God's grace upon him in the victory and the honor, he hastened to offer thanks to God in the form of peace offerings, which are sacrifices of shouting, and they are sacrifices that express man's love for God, accompanied by the blowing of trumpets, and offered at certain feasts. Likewise shouting and trumpets go before the soldiers returning victorious from war; therefore shouting accompanies the sacrifices (Num 10:10).

27.5.3.en: 3- The sacrifices of shouting that we offer in the New Testament to God, who gives us victory in our spiritual wars with the demons, are in the form of:

27.5.5.en: b - Humility before God and people.

27.5.6.en: c - Offering services to those around us.

27.5.7.en: d - Offering help to the poor and needy.

27.5.8.en: 4- In the end David declares his joy in the Lord by singing and chanting, that is, praising God in His house and in every place as an expression of his thanks to God. And this is what we do in the New Testament in the sacrifices of praise, and by this we pass from the bloody sacrifice to the sacrifice of the Eucharist, which is a sacrifice of thanksgiving and praise to God, accompanied by many praises.

27.5.9.en: Be steadfast in Christ your Rock, and fortify yourself in Him, and abide in His Church; then you will triumph over the demons, and live in constant joy and praise to God.

27.5.10.en: (3) Pleading for deliverance from the enemies (vv. 7-14).

27.6.0.en: 7- Hear, O LORD, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me.

27.6.1.en: 1- David asks God to hear his prayers, which he offered previously in the preceding verses, joined with the prayers of the believers who lift up their pleadings before God in His house. For he feels his membership in the house of the Lord, even if he is far from it because of his circumstances.

27.6.2.en: 2- In humility David says "have mercy upon me", that is, I do not deserve, O Lord, that You hear my prayer, but I am needy, so by Your mercy condescend and accept my prayers for my need of You.

27.7.0.en: 8- When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, "Thou saidst, Seek ye my face." Thy face, LORD, will I seek.

27.7.1.en: 1- David presents his request to God from his heart, that is, from the depths of his feelings and not only with his lips. And this is an expression of David's bond with the Person of God and his attachment to Him.

27.7.2.en: 2- God wishes that we love Him for His Person, and not merely as a means of fulfilling our requests, and David understood this; therefore he sought the face of God, that is, His Person, out of love for Him. He moved from asking for God's help against the enemies to being occupied with the face of God, because enjoying the presence of God is sweeter than anything in the world. And of course whoever feels the presence of God, God will not leave him but supplies all his needs; for Christ Himself said, "Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness" (Mt 6:33), and after this He will not neglect man but arranges for him the rest of the matters of his life, among them victory over the enemies.

27.7.3.en: 3- David sinned and repented of his sin, and kept making his bed swim with his tears every night, but his comfort - in the midst of these painful feelings, and in the midst of all his tribulations - is his enjoyment of seeing the face of God, who comforts him, satisfies him and gladdens him.

27.8.0.en: 9- Hide not thy face from me. Disappoint not thy servant in wrath: thou hast been my help; reject me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.

27.8.2.en: 1- While David is pursued by Saul and exposed to death at any moment, he was not distracted by this from seeking to see God; it is his life, which he cannot do without.

27.8.3.en: 2- David fears God, and this is shown by his caution and his fear of the wrath of God's justice; he is not careless if he has fallen into any sin, but lives always in the fear of God and guards against it, so he keeps away from sin.

27.8.4.en: 3- David's asking God not to hide His face from him shows his understanding that God hides His face from sinners; it is an implicit declaration of his repentance and his confession of his sin, but he hopes that God's mercy will forgive him and the recompense of his sins, that is, the wrath of God's justice, will not come upon him. He lives a life of repentance.

27.8.5.en: 4- David's saying "Disappoint not thy servant in wrath" shows his hope in God. In spite of David's confession of his sin, his hope is firm, so he asks with confidence for God's forgiveness and the enjoyment of seeing His face.

27.8.6.en: 5- David is accustomed to God's being his help; he lives in fellowship with God, therefore he asks God that this fellowship continue and not be cut off because of his sins, because he asks for God's forgiveness and mercy. And he asks God specifically not to reject him or forsake him, that is, he stresses the necessity that He establish him in Himself.

27.8.7.en: 6- David believes that his only salvation is from God, and he has no relation to any strange gods or human power; he trusts in God in everything, therefore he always receives his salvation.

27.9.0.en: 10- For my father and my mother have forsaken me, and the LORD embraces me.

27.9.1.en: 1- While David was fleeing from the face of Saul, his father and mother were of course not with him, but he had placed them with the king of Moab lest Saul harm them, so he means his deprivation of the care and support of his father and mother, especially as he suffers the pains of Saul's pursuit and evil. This suffering made him feel his need of the support of others, the most important of whom are the parents.

27.9.2.en: 2- The father and the mother represent the most important care a person receives, so David here means his deprivation, not only of father and mother, but also of the support of brothers, friends and loved ones; it is an expression of the extent of his suffering and endurance.

27.9.3.en: 3- If David was deprived of the care of the bodily father and mother, he powerfully enjoys the care of his spiritual Father, who is the Lord, who embraces him to His breast in tenderness and satisfies him with His love.

27.9.4.en: 4- If a person turns tribulation and material deprivation into a relationship with God, he experiences depths he never tasted before, and feels that the Lord embraces him, and this means:

27.9.5.en: a - That he is in God's embrace, that is, he feels His deep love.

27.9.6.en: b - That he has become one of God's own and has joined Him.

27.9.7.en: c - That he has been united with God by joining His embrace.

27.10.0.en: 11- Teach me thy way, O LORD, and lead me in a plain path, because of mine enemies.

27.10.1.en: 1- David's asking God to teach him His way and lead him in the straight path shows David's humility and his feeling as if he were a child who needs to learn how to walk. And of course he receives abundant divine guidance and grace.

27.10.2.en: 2- Saul, David's enemy, and all who were with him adopted evil methods to try to seize David, so David asks God for help, so that he is not influenced by or imitates the ways of evil, but that He teach him the straight way, built on the commandments of God.

27.10.3.en: 3- David did not ask for a way to triumph over his enemies, but asked for the straight way, that is, the divine way. And as long as he walks in the way of God, he is guaranteed His care and protection from all enemies. And above all this he keeps his peace and enjoys fellowship with God.

27.11.0.en: 12- Deliver me not over unto the will of them that trouble me: for false witnesses are risen up against me, and one that breathes out injustice.

27.11.1.en: One that breathes out: that is, who blows and sends out venom from his mouth like a serpent.

27.11.2.en: 1- David trusts in God's power; in spite of his weakness before Saul's armies, he believes in God's protection and His power, which is able to rescue him from the desire of his enemies who want to kill him.

27.11.3.en: 2- David's faith appears in his steadfastness and his confidence in God who is with him, in spite of the rising up against him of false witnesses, who are Saul's followers, who made many false claims against him, such as his rebellion against the king, or his refusal of worship of God in His house, or his union with the enemies of Israel such as the Philistines, and all this is false; because of the violence of Saul's pursuit, David was compelled at times to flee to the Philistines, but he still held fast to the worship of God, as appeared from the preceding verses in this Psalm.

27.11.4.en: 3- If the enemies relied on breathing out their venom like serpents, in the lies they let loose and in their attempts to kill David, David on the other hand relied on God, who is able to deliver him from their hands.

27.12.0.en: 13- Had I not believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.

27.12.1.en: The goodness of the Lord: His grace and kindnesses.

27.12.2.en: 1- In the midst of the many tribulations that David suffers, he believed in God's grace and goodness, and that He is able to solve his problems.

27.12.3.en: 2- The land of the living does not mean only our earth on which we live, but also the heavenly Jerusalem. For in the midst of tribulations David believed that God would compensate him for his suffering with rest and glories in heaven.

27.12.4.en: 3- David was preoccupied with the heavenly glories that he sees while on earth more than with all his problems, and this gave him comfort, peace and strength to bear the sufferings. In the midst of the tribulation he is occupied with God and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him more than with solving his problems.

27.13.0.en: 14- Wait for the LORD; let your heart be strengthened and take courage, and wait for the LORD.

27.13.1.en: 1- At the end of the Psalm David addresses everyone who loves God, and even addresses himself also, to wait for the Lord during his suffering in tribulation, because the Lord is without doubt coming. Faith in God's love and concern gives rest to the heart, so it does not find the tribulation heavy.

27.13.2.en: 2- Waiting for the Lord means the necessity of patience and accepting tribulation for a time. This is by God's permission for the benefit and good of man, for we do not obtain good except by patience.

27.13.3.en: 3- Tribulation may be prolonged and may continue throughout life, so a person must wait, and his comfort is God's grace, to which he referred in the preceding verse. Perhaps for this reason he repeated the words "wait for the LORD" at the beginning of the verse and at its end.

27.13.4.en: 4- The devil sends fears during the tribulation to weaken a person, so that he gives way to despair and depression and abandons his spiritual striving, so David calls to him to be strengthened and take courage, to triumph in the spiritual war and come out of the tribulation victorious.

27.13.5.en: 5- David experienced this waiting practically in his life; he was anointed king at about the age of sixteen, but did not reign until the age of thirty over one tribe, the tribe of Judah, then at the age of thirty-seven he reigned over the rest of the tribes; and he wished and waited to build a house for the Lord, but God prevented him and told him that his son is the one who would build it, so he accepted this with thanks from God's hand, and prepared all he could for building the house.

27.13.6.en: Do not fear tribulation, for its appearance at the beginning seems hard. But be sure that inside its bitterness is a wonderful sweetness, and an experience of God that you have not tasted before, so persevere in your striving, confident of God's help and His comforts. A cry to God the Almighty. Of David. "Unto thee will I cry, O LORD" (v. 1). Introduction:

27.13.7.en: 1- Its writer is David the prophet, as appears from its title.

27.13.9.en: He wrote it when he was fleeing either from the face of Saul or from the face of his son Absalom, as shown by his aversion to the deceitful wicked, declaring his rejection of the treachery that Absalom committed (v. 3).

27.13.10.en: 3- It is considered one of the messianic Psalms, because it speaks about Christ the Savior, who intercedes for His children by His pure blood for ever (vv. 8, 9).

27.13.11.en: 4- This Psalm suits every believer who suffers tribulations, and also suits the suffering Church in her cry to God.

27.13.12.en: 5- This Psalm is not found among the Psalms of the Agpeya.
